course.lead: Short everyday conversations, A1 to A2. Each one has three stars: read it, say it from prompts, then from memory.

conversation.howToRead: it is spelt the English way, with the stressed syllable in CAPITALS (Polish stresses the last syllable but one). “zh” is the s in “measure”; “y” as in “yes”; “i” as in “bit”; “ee” as in “see”; “oo” as in “too”; “h” is breathier, like the ch in “loch”.
conversation.leaveBody: Your progress is saved. You can finish it today from Home.

speech.howWeCountBody: A line counts when enough of its words were said and you added no extra words. The first try needs 90% of the words, the second 80%, and every try after that 70% — so a short line may need every word at first. Recognition slips are forgiven: missing Polish letters, one letter off in a longer word, a word split in two or two run together.

settings.about: Fluentum {{version}} — free, no ads, runs entirely in your browser.
settings.backupHint: All data lives only on this device. A backup keeps it safe and lets you move it.
settings.characterHint: Choose the figure that stands for you in Fluentum.
settings.checkingHint: Every try of a line is gentler than the one before: the first needs 90% of its words, the second 80%, and from the third on 70%. A word heard as a different one counts as not said; a word added to the line still fails the try.
settings.dayStartHint: Practising after midnight still counts for the previous day until this hour.
settings.displayNameHint: Friends see it on their leaderboard. Empty = your character's name.
settings.engineHint: Automatic uses the browser’s own recognition (Web Speech) and switches to offline Whisper where there is none (e.g. Firefox).
settings.handsFreeHint: Keep listening through the whole conversation and check each line as you speak.
settings.installBody: Put Fluentum on your home screen: it opens full-screen like an app, starts faster and works offline.
settings.installDone: Fluentum is on your home screen.
settings.languageHint: Fluentum speaks to you in your language and practises the other one with you.
settings.listenFirstHint: Fluentum reads each of your lines aloud before you say it — a great way to catch the pronunciation.
settings.privacyHint: No account, no server, no tracking. Your progress stays in this browser.
settings.reminderHint: Fluentum has no server to send notifications, so the reminder lives in your phone’s calendar — reliable and free.
settings.saveTranscriptsHint: Store what was recognised with each attempt. When off, only the result is kept. Audio is never stored.
settings.soundsHint: A soft chime for every line said; a fuller one for a finished conversation or goal.
settings.title: Settings
settings.whisperConfirmBody: Fluentum will download about {{size}} once: the model from Hugging Face (huggingface.co) and the speech engine from Fluentum’s site. On mobile data this can be costly — use Wi-Fi if you can. Afterwards recognition works offline and your audio never leaves the device.
settings.whisperDone: Whisper is ready — it works offline now
settings.whisperFailed: The download failed. Check your connection and try again.
settings.whisperIntro: Recognises speech right on this device: 100% private — the audio never leaves it — and it works in Firefox too. It is slower than the browser’s recognition, especially on older phones, and checks each line after you finish it (no live listening).
settings.whisperModelHint: Base (recommended) recognises speech much better; Tiny is smaller and faster but makes more mistakes.
settings.whisperNeedsDownload: Download the model to use Whisper.
settings.whisperNoSpace: There isn’t enough storage space on this device for the model.
settings.whisperUnavailable: This browser can’t run Whisper (it needs Web Workers, WebAssembly, offline storage and microphone recording).
settings.wordColoursHint: Colour the subject, predicate, adjectives and objects of every line, with their counterparts in the translation.

data.lead: Everything you do in Fluentum is stored only in this browser on this device — no account, no server. A backup is a file you keep somewhere else and can restore on any device.
data.passwordWarning: Write the password down somewhere safe. Without it the backup cannot be restored — nobody, not even Fluentum's author, can recover it for you.
data.previewLess: This backup holds less progress than this device.
data.previewOlder: This backup is older than the data on this device — the later days will be replaced.
data.previewReplace: The data on this device will be replaced with the backup.
data.previewUndo: The current data is kept on this device — you can undo the restore under “Your data”.
data.protectHint: A backup holds your whole learning history. With a password nobody can read it — not in the cloud, not in your mail.

data.redoConfirmTitle: Go back to the restored backup's data?
data.restoreHint: Replaces the data on this device with a backup file. You will see what the file holds before anything is replaced, and the data from before the restore stays here — you can undo it.
data.share: Save to the cloud or send

data.storageOn: The browser protects this data and will not delete it on its own. A backup still matters: a new phone, a cleared browser or a broken device.

support.line: Fluentum is free, with no ads and no tracking. If it helps you, you can buy its author a coffee.
support.note: buycoffee.to · opens in a new tab
support.strip: Fluentum is free · buy the author a coffee
support.tip1: Say each line at your own pace. I wait for you — never the other way round.
support.tip10: Words said aloud stay with you longer than words only read.
support.tip2: Five to fifteen minutes a day is the golden quarter-hour: enough to grow, short enough to keep.
support.tip3: Mispronounced a word? Tap “Listen”, copy the melody, and say it again. Parrots learn this way too.
support.tip4: Read a conversation first, then try it with prompts the next day: your memory loves a short break.
support.tip5: Same time, same place: a habit grows best in the same soil.
support.tip6: Recall mode is the real thing: you know what you want to say — now say it in the other language.
support.tip7: A streak freeze covers a missed day. Rest does not undo the way you have come.
support.tip8: Tap a coloured word to see its partner in the translation: grammar is easier when you can see it.
support.tip9: Say the line as if you meant it. Real intonation sticks better than a careful whisper.
